summary: Practise adverse-event assessment, ICSR workflows, signal escalation, and quality controls. Explore this five-day pharmacovigilance course.
lede: Pharmacovigilance training helps medicine safety teams manage suspected adverse reaction reports from intake through documented assessment. Designed for safety officers, case processors, pharmacy leads and programme staff, it develops skills in case validation, seriousness and causality assessment, and follow-up planning. Practical exercises also cover narrative preparation, electronic ICSR workflows, quality checks and signal escalation, with templates for adapting processes to institutional responsibilities.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who receive, assess, report, oversee, or support medicine safety cases. It is suitable for people working with institutional pharmacovigilance processes and reporting responsibilities.
prerequisites: Prior work with medicine safety reporting, pharmacy operations, regulatory responsibilities, or quality processes is useful. No coding is required. Bring a laptop if you wish to work with digital case-tracking templates; no specific software installation is assumed.
